title: Moon Gate Garden
description: The front garden and driveway needed more than just another average lawn. This front garden aims to combine different aspects, including aesthetics and sustainability, to buffer a fire-prone hazardous area, privacy, and ultimately a front garden that the family can be part of, every time they leave and come back home. The lush, mostly native planting works well as it provides privacy, enhancing and featuring the existing Takuroo trees. They also offer a bit of mystery to the ones who walk past and look through the shades of greens and the moongate itself. The curved lines, to contrast the harsh geometric lines of the house, offer a sense of natural flow, guiding you through the garden and taking you to the next wonder. This front garden also works as a buffer to the fire-prone natural reserve nearby, protecting the house and people around. A family garden that can also be shared by the community, feeding the natural local flora and fauna.
